result:
Read the chicken edit against the ledger and the guide. Short version: this is not tidying, but it is not new either — it is the fourth time he has done the same thing.

**What the edit actually is.** 24 pixels, all of them erased. Nothing added, nothing recoloured, no colour introduced to or removed from the sheet. Every one of the eight bounding boxes sits at y=14–15 of a 16-pixel cell — the bottom one or two rows, 2 to 4 pixels wide, under the bird. Same evening he did Crow (y=14–15, same band) and Neighbour (y=39–45, x=20–27 of a 48-pixel cell — dead centre bottom, under the feet). Three actors, one sitting, one band.

**What it repeats.** Every hand edit in the whole ledger — seven sheets — is erase-only. `colors_added` is empty in every single entry. The four he bothered to annotate all say the same sentence in different words: *white cells that should have been transparent so you can see what's behind.* Cream `#f8f4e6` is the shared highlight in our generated palette and is already documented in CREDITS as a colour the pipeline mishandles. On a pale chicken that stray cream reads as body rather than as a defect, which is probably why it survived to the build.

**What it tells me about the direction, which is the part worth the session.** He is protecting the ground plane. An actor in this game stands on a tile whose state — tilled, watered, ripe — is information the player has to read, and a two-pixel opaque skirt under a walking bird hides that square and *slides* as the bird walks, so the same tile reads differently depending on where the chicken is standing. The rule his hand is writing: an actor never occludes the square it stands on with anything but its own body. The silhouette flag fired on all eight frames, so this did change the outline — but he did it frame by frame, consistently across the walk and its mirror, and the cycle's bob is intact.

**Against the guide.** No contradiction, because the guide has nothing to contradict. It covers ramps, coloured outlines, saturation-pop and reserved hues; it says nothing about where a sprite ends and the ground begins, and the renderer draws no contact shadow. That is a hole, and it is the one thing he has now fixed by hand on three actors in one evening. Second thing for the session: he has never once touched a colour. Q-14 asks about palette personality and his own strokes give zero evidence either way — that question still has to be asked with pictures, not read off the ledger.

One measurement I could not take here: I can read the before/after PNGs but not decode them, so "the erased pixels were cream" is inference from the pattern and the palette, not verified. Ravi's check below produces the real number.

**What your yes starts.** The headline is not the chicken — it is that he has now hand-cleaned the same pipeline defect four times, which is a manual step he keeps performing. Accepting this puts the detection into the asset pipeline so he stops finding them, and files the ground-line observation into the material for the style session rather than into the unsigned guide.

Crow/Chicken/Neighbour on 2026-09-16) is erase-only — colors_added empty every time, never a recolour — and the 16 Sep batch all cluster in the bottom 1–2 rows under the feet. The rule his hand writes: an actor never occludes the tile it stands on with anything but its own body. The unsigned style guide has no rule about the sprite/ground boundary, and his edits give no evidence at all on palette personality (Q-14).</remember>
